items.definition:
to inform someone
Please notify me if there are any changes.

to give new strength or energy to
A cold drink will refresh you.

set again
I need to reset my password.

move or travel very quickly; adjust a camera lens
The car zoomed past us.

admit or acknowledge
He decided to confess his crime.

organize; work together
We need to coordinate our efforts to finish the project on time.

to convince someone to do something
I tried to persuade her to come with us.

to cease to be valid, typically after a fixed period of time; to die
My passport will expire next year.

to force liquid or gas to move
The heart is constantly pumping blood around the body.

to damage or ruin
Don't spoil the surprise for him.

burst or cause to burst with a loud noise and force
The fireworks exploded in the night sky.

to clean or empty with a rush of water; to turn red in the face
Don't forget to flush the toilet. Her face began to flush with embarrassment.

to reduce to the smallest possible amount or degree
We need to minimize the risks.

cause sharp pain
A bee stung me on the arm.

make a regular sound; mark
The clock began to tick loudly.

walk aimlessly
We decided to wander around the old town.

work together
We need to cooperate to finish this project on time.

pause before acting or speaking
Don't hesitate to ask if you have any questions.

mark or discolor with something that is not easily removed
Be careful not to stain your new shirt.

suffer or die from hunger
Many people in the region are starving due to the drought.

leave, especially to start a journey
The train will depart from platform 3.

to move forward on the hands and knees or by dragging the body close to the ground
The baby learned to crawl at six months old.

to die through submersion in and inhalation of water
He was careful not to drown while swimming in the deep end.

to pass the tongue over
The dog started to lick its paw.

to move in a circle around a central axis
The Earth rotates on its axis once every 24 hours.

make (beer, coffee, or tea) by soaking, boiling, and fermentation
I'll brew some fresh coffee for us.

to grip tightly between the thumb and a finger
She pinched herself to make sure she wasn't dreaming.

to expect or believe; to calculate
I reckon it's going to rain soon.

to promote a product or service
Companies advertise their products on TV.

move or fall downwards
The plane began to descend towards the airport.

to surround or close off
Please enclose the documents in the envelope.

to make someone afraid
The loud noise frightened the cat.

to delay
We had to postpone the meeting until next week.

be exceptionally good at or proficient in an activity or subject
She always strives to excel in her studies.

to become smaller
My sweater will shrink if I wash it in hot water.

to remove a cover from; to discover
They hope to uncover the truth.

to make or become weak
The storm began to weaken as it moved inland.

to have difficulty breathing because of something in your throat
He started to choke on a piece of food.

pull (something) behind
The truck had to tow the broken-down car.

disappear suddenly
The magician made the rabbit vanish from the hat.

gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of
Dust tends to accumulate in corners.

love and respect deeply
I adore my grandchildren.

be cautious and alert to risks or dangers
Beware of the dog.

arrange for compensation in the event of damage to or loss of property
You should insure your car against theft.

make something easier to understand or do
Please simplify the instructions.

to plan and direct the route or course of a ship, aircraft, or other form of transport, especially by using instruments or maps
It's difficult to navigate without a map.

to express disapproval of someone or something
It's easy to criticise others, but harder to offer solutions.

to remove marks or information
Please erase the whiteboard before you leave.

to make fabric by interlocking loops of yarn
My grandmother loves to knit sweaters.

to pay back (a loan, debt, or money)
He promised to repay the loan by next month.

to make something completely wet
Let the clothes soak in water before washing them.

to trip or lose one's balance; to make a mistake
He stumbled over a loose rock and almost fell.

to marry (someone)
They plan to wed next spring.

to cut with a sharp blade
He used a knife to slash the rope.

to move or cause to move slowly to and fro
The trees swayed gently in the breeze.

to behave as if attracted to someone
He likes to flirt with all the waitresses.

to look at something closely, typically to assess its condition or discover any shortcomings
The mechanic will inspect the car for any damage.

eject matter from the stomach through the mouth
He felt sick and had to vomit.

make or become larger
Can you enlarge this photo for me?

to push, fold, or turn something into a small space
She tucked the blanket around the baby.

to annoy or make angry; to make sore or inflamed
His constant complaining really started to irritate me.

to look through a number of books or magazines without reading everything; to look at goods in a shop without necessarily buying anything; to look at information on the internet
I like to browse in bookstores.

to jab or prod
He poked me with his elbow.

to post something again, especially on social media
Please don't repost my photos without permission.
